title: Module sheafification commutes with underlying sets on a sieve site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$: a sieve on an object is a set of arrows to it closed under precomposition, and covering sieves are stable under pullback and transitive and include maximal sieves. Use universes [def-weil-size-convention] large enough for sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $P:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda$ be a presheaf. Write $P^\#$ for its sheafification with values in $\Lambda$-modules, and $|P|$ for its underlying presheaf of sets. There is a natural isomorphism $(|P|)^\#\cong|P^\#|$ commuting with the maps from $|P|$; equivalently, the underlying set map of the module sheafification unit exhibits the sheafification of the underlying set presheaf. No fibre products in $\mathcal C$ or subcanonical topology are assumed.

mathlib_match.how: Specialize sheafifyComposeIso at lines 233-236 and sheafComposeIso_hom_fac at lines 239-242 to F := forget (ModuleCat Λ). The concrete forgetful PreservesSheafification instance at lines 305-314 applies because module forgetful functors preserve limits and filtered colimits and reflect isomorphisms. The comparison is natural in P and its unit equation is precisely the stated compatibility. Instance details read: ModuleCat.forget_preservesLimits (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Limits.lean:181-182), ModuleCat.forget_preservesFilteredColimits (FilteredColimits.lean:202-204), and the anonymous forgetful ReflectsIsomorphisms instance (Basic.lean:616-620). CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hasSheafCompose_of_preservesLimitsOfSize (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Whiskering.lean:161-163) supplies HasSheafCompose. Take module/set value universes at least as large as the site and the ring; these are instance hypotheses, not extra geometric assumptions.
